Murafa Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Murafa, whose Jewish community was tied administratively to Dzhuryn's, documented elsewhere in this collection, was so overwhelmingly Jewish by 1897 that Old Murafa alone counted 1,350 Jews out of 1,361 total residents — one of the highest concentrations recorded anywhere in this collection. The community survived Haidamak violence in 1735 before a 1941 Nazi occupation and subsequent Transnistria annexation brought a ghetto absorbing thousands of deportees from Bessarabia and Bukovina; 2,605 remained by September 1943. Around 600 Jews had returned to Murafa by 1946. This cemetery, established in the 16th century, remains in use today, with about 3,000 surviving headstones.
